items.title: Brent pushed back above USD 101 on Wednesday - a second straight gain
items.summary: Brent settled around USD 101.6 on Wednesday 23 September, up about 2.4 percent on the day and the second consecutive rise, with the month-to-date gain near 10 percent. Two things held it there: the strait is still effectively shut, and the US-Iran channel produced no confirmed progress. One new detail matters more than the price print - Iran's port authority has blacklisted 77 vessels for using the southern corridor without paying tolls, most of them tankers, and the blacklist does not appear to be deterring traffic. The closure is now producing revenue for Tehran rather than being a chip it wants to spend. For OD1: the price that will decide the 2027 revenue line is being set by an arrangement that has started to pay for itself.
items.source: TradingEconomics Brent series, 23 Sep 2026 (101.61, +2.37 pct day, +10.24 pct month). Windward Daily Intelligence (77-vessel toll blacklist; tankers 85 pct of the list; 40 pct Emirati-owned or chartered). W=2 origins for the price path; the blacklist is W=1 and flagged as such. Anti-thesis search for a materially softer 2027 view was run and is recorded in the 2027 price-band item below - it did not falsify the near-term reading, it bounded it.

items.title: Hormuz shut on day 207; the seven-day offer still has no taker and no confirmation
items.summary: The latest recorded transit count is a single vessel on 20 September against roughly 85 on a normal day, so the strait remains effectively closed to commercial shipping. Iran's 22 September offer to reopen within seven days remains conditional on Washington easing military pressure and lifting the blockade of Iranian ports, and it still sits beside Tehran's standing position that reopening is ruled out until six demands are met. No Omani confirmation and no US response. Treat it as a negotiating position, not a schedule.
items.source: straits.live daily brief 23 Sep 2026 (day 206-207; IMF PortWatch one transit on 20 Sep against pre-crisis baseline). Prior register entry for the 22 Sep seven-day offer (Reuters, 22 Sep). Two Iranian positions, no counterparty confirmation - CONTESTED stands. W=2.

items.title: The 2027 oil price the budget is built on is now under upward review
items.summary: Reported on 22 September: the government's existing oil forecasts assume Brent averaging USD 80 a barrel in 2026 and USD 74 in 2027, and those assumptions are under review for upward revision to roughly USD 90 and USD 80. That is the line that decides petroleum revenue in Budget 2027, tabled on 9 October. Against it stands the outside view: the EIA expects Brent to average USD 74 in 2027 as inventories rebuild, Wood Mackenzie models USD 78 on reopening, and JPMorgan points at the low USD 60s from the second half of 2027. So the official assumption is being revised up at exactly the moment the mine-run forecasters see the price coming down. For OD1 that gap - not the daily price - is the thing to watch: a budget built on USD 80 to 90 revenue is a different employer balance sheet from one built on USD 74.
items.source: BusinessToday.my 22 Sep 2026 (base assumptions USD 80 / USD 74, under review toward about USD 90 / USD 80); EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook (Brent averaging USD 74 in 2027); Wood Mackenzie via AOGR (USD 78 in 2027 on reopening); J.P. Morgan Global Research (low USD 60s from H2 2027). Four origins, each labelled; the official review figure is a single reported source and is marked as reported. Chronological lock: published assumptions before 22 Sep < review reported 22 Sep < budget tabling 9 Oct 2026.

items.title: Budget 2027 is 15 days out - GST return ruled out, the oil assumption is the live variable

Watch whether the oil price assumption is formally raised from its published base, and whether the fuel subsidy framework is restated.

items.title: CORRECTION: the Fed raised rates to 3.75-4.00 percent on 16 September - the register had this as stalled
items.summary: The FOMC raised the target range by 25 basis points to 3.75 to 4.00 percent on 16 September, on a 12-0 vote, effective 17 September, and the September projections put the funds rate in the low 4 percent range in 2027. The register recorded no new development in the window; that was wrong - the decision landed on the 16th, before the last two sweeps. The correction is recorded here rather than smoothed over. What it means for OD1 is unchanged in kind and larger in size: a higher-for-longer US path feeds the ringgit, imported cost and LNG contracting economics, and firms the USD leg of every dollar-denominated figure in the budget and MSS stack.
items.source: federalreserve.gov press release 16 Sep 2026 (raise, 12-0) and implementation note effective 17 Sep (target range 3-3/4 to 4 percent); FOMC projections 16 Sep 2026; Chair Warsh press conference transcript 16 Sep 2026. One origin - the Federal Reserve itself - across three primary documents, so W=1 with high warrant. Correction recorded by appending, not by editing the earlier entry.

items.title: Haze reverses: Sarawak back to very unhealthy - Kanowit 244, Serian 201 by 6pm
items.summary: After two days of improvement, readings turned back up on Wednesday 23 September. Kanowit recorded 244 in the morning and was still very unhealthy at midday; Serian recorded 201 as of 6pm, and around a dozen other Sarawak stations sat in the unhealthy band, including Kuching 175, Sibu 171, Sarikei 169 and Bintulu 169. The peninsula remains outside the unhealthy band and no warning-level alert applies to Kuala Muda. No emergency threshold has been declared anywhere, and the snapshots differ by time of day, so read the readings with their timestamps.
items.source: Malay Mail 23 Sep 2026 (Kanowit 244 then 208; Lubok Antu 205 then 195); The Star 23 Sep 6pm (Serian 201, 12 others unhealthy); FMT 23 Sep (Serian 201 at 6pm; Kuching 175, Sibu 171, Sarikei 169, Bintulu 169); Bernama 23 Sep 9am (13 areas unhealthy, highest 180). items.title: The physical unwind still starts before the cost unwind - watch the freight and premium legs
items.summary: No new trigger this sweep, but the mechanism is worth keeping visible: war-risk premiums and LNG freight reprice on exposure windows, so they unwind over weeks to quarters after a trigger event, not in the same session. Concrete consequence: if reopening talk firms, expect Brent to fall before PETRONAS's delivered-cost base does - a margin squeeze that shows up in the trading and LNG books after the crisis has left the front page. And the reverse holds: with the closure now paying Tehran tolls, the trigger may be slower to arrive than the headline cycle suggests.
items.source: Mechanism documented in prior editions' insurance-market sourcing; today's supporting facts are the toll blacklist (Windward, 23 Sep) and the still-shut strait (straits.live, 23 Sep). W=2.

items.title: EPF nomination voids on change of marital status - check it once, before OD1, not after
items.summary: A change in marital status voids an existing EPF nomination, and the money then distributes by faraid and probate rules rather than your written choice. Concrete consequence: in an exit year with a lump sum touching EPF-adjacent planning, an outdated nomination is a silent failure that only surfaces at the worst moment. One portal check, five minutes. Carries forward.

items.title: The first stellar stream found outside our galaxy - pulled out of old Hubble data
items.summary: Astronomers identified the first globular-cluster stellar stream beyond the Milky Way: a faint ribbon of stars trailing from an ancient cluster around the ultra-diffuse galaxy UGC 9050-Dw1, about 115 million light-years away. Stellar streams trace a galaxy's gravity, so this one gave the team a way to weigh dark matter in a galaxy far outside our own. The find came out of the Hubble archive - the data already existed.
items.source: Nature 2026 (s41586-026-10878-w); ScienceDaily 21-23 Sep 2026; EurekAlert release. W=2 (paper plus release). Checkable against the Nature paper.

items.title: Webb found water surviving beside the Milky Way's black hole
items.summary: Using JWST, astronomers detected oxygen-rich dust and water in the extreme environment around Sagittarius A*, the supermassive black hole at the centre of our galaxy - the first water detection there. Molecular material is surviving radiation intense enough to be expected to destroy it, which means stars close to the black hole can keep feeding material back into their surroundings.
items.source: ESA/Webb release weic2617; Space.com 23 Sep 2026; Earth.com 13 Sep 2026. W=2 (ESA primary plus broadcaster).

items.title: Titanosaurs nested far south of the equator, eggshells show
items.summary: Fossil eggshells place titanosaur nesting grounds far south of the equator, widening the known breeding range of the long-necked giants. Nesting sites are how you reconstruct where these animals actually lived and moved, rather than where their bones happened to fossilise.
items.source: Sci.News 22 Sep 2026 (Paleontology), reporting the eggshell study. W=1 flagged; checkable against the underlying paper.
